topic: Yale David Geffen School of Drama, Acting MFA: public-domain Greek play texts for scene study (DRAM 293b The Greeks), Yale Cabaret and Summer Cabaret, filmed monologues and showcase, required supplies (2026-2027)

findings.what: DRAM 293b The Greeks: description (2026-2027 Bulletin)
findings.value: Second-year scene-study module running alongside the final six weeks of Plays of Extended and Heightened Language; scenes from classical Greek texts in translation and/or modern poetic adaptations, prepared and rehearsed for presentation in class. Instructor Evan Yionoulis.
findings.quote: DRAM 293b, The Greeks The purpose of second-year scene study is to continue to develop the actor's ability to embody and activate heightened circumstances and poetic text. This module runs alongside the final six weeks of Plays of Extended and Heightened Language and is centered on scenes from classical Greek texts in translation and/or modern poetic adaptations. Students prepare and rehearse scenes for presentation and exploration in class. Evan Yionoulis

findings.what: Scene 1: Sophocles, Antigone — first Creon–Antigone confrontation (Jebb)
findings.value: Creon and Antigone alone after the Guard exits; lines 441-525, from Creon's 'do you admit, or deny' to 'While I live, no woman will rule me' (Ismene is sent for next)
findings.quote: You, you with your face bent to the ground, do you admit, or deny that you did this? ... While I live, no woman will rule me. [525]

findings.what: Scene 2: Sophocles, Oedipus Tyrannus — Oedipus–Teiresias (Jebb)
findings.value: Oedipus and Teiresias; lines 300-462, from Oedipus' opening address to Teiresias' parting challenge
findings.quote: Teiresias, whose soul grasps all things, both that which may be told and that which is unspeakable ... So go in and evaluate this, and if you find that I am wrong, say then that I have no wit in prophecy.

findings.what: Scene 3: Sophocles, Electra — Electra–Chrysothemis, the first sisters' scene (Jebb)
findings.value: Electra and Chrysothemis (Chorus has a few lines); about lines 328-471, from Chrysothemis' entrance to her exit with the offerings
findings.quote: let me have your silence, [470] since if my mother hears of it, I believe that this attempt which I will dare shall in the end cause me bitterness. Exit Chrysothemis on the spectators' right.

findings.what: Scene 4: Euripides, Medea — first Jason–Medea confrontation (Murray)
findings.value: Jason and Medea (the Leader speaks twice); Jason's entrance through Medea's last reply before the Aegeus scene; Greek lines ~446-626 (line numbers from Perseus' Kovacs text, which is not PD; use Murray's PD text to perform)
findings.quote: _Enter from the right_ JASON. JASON. Oft have I seen, in other days than these, How a dark temper maketh maladies No friend can heal.

findings.what: Scene 4 line anchor: Medea, Jason's entrance at line 446
findings.value: Lines 446-491 card begins with Jason's entrance speech; Jason and Medea speak
findings.quote: Not now for the first time but often before I have seen what an impossible evil to deal with is a fierce temper.

findings.what: Scene 5: Euripides, Bacchae — Pentheus interrogates the bound Stranger (Dionysus) (Murray; Buckley for line numbers)
findings.value: Pentheus and Dionysus in stichomythia; Greek lines ~451-518 (Buckley card: Pentheus' questioning begins 454, Dionysus led off 515-518); Murray's PD verse text has the same scene
findings.quote: [_The guards loose the arms of_ DIONYSUS; PENTHEUS _studies him for a while in silence, then speaks jeeringly_. DIONYSUS _remains gentle and unafraid_.

findings.what: Scene 5 line anchor: Bacchae, end of the Pentheus–Dionysus exchange (Buckley)
findings.value: Dionysus' exit lines about 515-518
findings.quote: I will go, for I need not suffer that which is not necessary. But Dionysus, who you claim does not exist, will pursue you for these insults.

findings.what: Scene 6: Aeschylus, Agamemnon — the tapestry (carpet) scene, Clytemnestra–Agamemnon (Murray; Smyth for line numbers)
findings.value: Clytemnestra and Agamemnon; Clytemnestra enters with the tapestries at about line 855 (Smyth places the entrance direction near 850), Agamemnon agrees to tread the purple at 957-958 and goes in; Smyth marks his entry to the palace and Clytemnestra's exit at about 970-974. Murray's PD verse text has the same scene.
findings.quote: I will tread upon a purple pathway as I pass to my palace halls.

findings.what: Scene 6 in Murray's text: Agamemnon tapestry moment
findings.value: Murray's stage direction and Agamemnon's yielding lines
findings.quote: [_The attendants spread tapestries of crimson and gold from the Chariot to the Door of the Palace._ AGAMEMNON _does not move_.]

findings.what: Yale Cabaret: strictly extracurricular for actors; chair approves participation
findings.value: Extracurricular; Acting chair works with Cabaret artistic directors on approval; depends on casting obligations and academic standing
findings.quote: Yale Cabaret provides an additional, although strictly extracurricular, outlet for the exploration of a wide range of material, including self-scripted pieces, company-devised original work, adaptations, and musicals. The program's chair works directly with the Yale Cabaret artistic directors regarding approval of Cabaret participation by actors. Participation in Yale Cabaret productions is dependent on students' program-related casting obligations and academic standing.

findings.what: Yale Cabaret: participation rules (encouraged, ranks 6th of 7 in scheduling priority, advance chair approval for Acting, none on academic warning)
findings.value: Encouraged but voluntary; conflicts never resolved in the Cabaret's favour; Acting and Directing chairs must approve in advance; students on academic warning may not participate
findings.quote: Students in all programs are encouraged to involve themselves in the Yale Cabaret ... Conflicts with these priorities will not be resolved in favor of the cabaret. ... approval from the chairs of the following academic programs is required in advance before a student commits to participation in the Yale Cabaret: Directing and Acting. ... No student on academic warning in any program may participate in the cabaret.

findings.what: Scheduling priority of Yale Cabaret
findings.value: 6th of 7 priorities (after Yale Rep calls, classes, ticketed School productions, other assigned projects, required work-study)
findings.quote: 6. Yale Cabaret productions, which are extracurricular 7. Any formally approved outside work, affinity group meetings, events, or productions, and elective work-study

findings.what: Yale Cabaret: student-run, actors may direct
findings.value: Own student artistic and management leadership reporting to a board; entirely student-produced; only place students regularly leave their discipline
findings.quote: With its own student artistic and management leadership, reporting to a board of directors comprising students, faculty, staff, and New Haven community members, the Yale Cabaret presents work that is entirely student-produced. It is the only area of production at the School where students regularly move out of their primary discipline of study: actors may direct, managers act, playwrights produce.

findings.what: Yale Cabaret: acting program page note on double casting
findings.value: Actors who are double cast may not do Cabaret shows
findings.quote: Actors who are double cast may not participate in Yale Cabaret productions.

findings.what: Yale Cabaret: performance pattern (2024-25 season report)
findings.value: New show each weekend, Thursday-Saturday 8 p.m. plus 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday; 15 shows that season plus a two-production Ignite Festival
findings.quote: Each weekend of the Cab's demanding season presents a new show Thursday through Saturday at 8 p.m., and at 11 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays.

findings.what: Yale Cabaret: shows per season (2024-25)
findings.quote: 15 shows — including the annual Dragaret, a celebration of cross-gender performance

findings.what: Yale Summer Cabaret: student-run summer theater
findings.value: Student-run and interdisciplinary; a new artistic and management team each season
findings.quote: During the summer, Yale Summer Cabaret is the exploratory theatrical home for David Geffen School of Drama students. Like Yale Cabaret, it is student-run and interdisciplinary. Each season, a new artistic and management team has the opportunity to shape the theater's vision

findings.what: Yale Summer Cabaret leadership (2026)
findings.value: Co-artistic directors from Lighting and Projection Design MFA programs; producing director (2nd-year Theater Management); managing director (3rd-year Theater Management); season 'Spectra'
findings.quote: Spectra, a season dedicated to exploring accessibility, innovation, and community through the performing arts.

findings.what: DRAM 463a/b On-Camera Acting Technique (third year)
findings.value: Three-session course; brief scenes of the student's choice filmed, watched, discussed, refilmed. Ellen Novack.
findings.quote: DRAM 463a/b, On-Camera Acting Technique This three-session course gives students experience working on camera. Brief scenes of the individual student's choice are filmed, watched, discussed, and, when time permits, filmed again.

findings.what: DRAM 473b Taming the Cyclops: professionally shot film monologues posted on the School website
findings.value: Film/TV monologue rehearsed over two classes, shot with a professional cinematographer, edited professionally, posted on the School website at the end of the final semester; also industry workshops and self-tape audition practice. Ellen Novack.
findings.quote: with the help of a professional cinematographer and their equipment, each student's monologue is shot in a situation that mimics a professional shoot as closely as possible. The monologues are edited professionally and posted on the School website at the end of the final semester, so casting directors, representatives, and other professionals can experience our students' work on camera.

findings.what: DRAM 793b Actor Showcase
findings.value: Final-term scenes presented to industry in New York and Los Angeles; directed by Paul Mullins; Incompletes must be cleared by week four of the final semester to be eligible
findings.quote: DRAM 793b, Actor Showcase In their final term, students choose and rehearse scenes, which are presented to agents, managers, casting directors, and other members of the industry in New York and Los Angeles.
